nations.name: Hla'alua
nations.lands: Taoyuan and Namaxia districts, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: In 2014 the Hla'alua were officially recognized as a distinct people, becoming the 15th Indigenous people listed in Taiwan.
The Hla'alua are formed by four communities, Paiciana, Vilanganʉ, Talicia and Hlihlara, in Kaohsiung City.

nations.name: Ainu
nations.lands: Hokkaido and other parts of Japan

facts.text: Upopoy, a national centre for Ainu history and culture in Shiraoi, Hokkaido, opened to the public in July 2020.

source.title: About Upopoy
source.publisher: Upopoy National Ainu Museum and Park

facts.text: A 2019 Japanese law names the Ainu as an Indigenous people of northern Japan, especially Hokkaido, and aims for a society that respects Ainu pride.

source.title: Act on Promoting Measures to Achieve a Society in which the Pride of Ainu People is Respected (Act No. 16 of 2019)
source.publisher: Japanese Law Translation, Ministry of Justice, Japan

nations.name: Sherpa
nations.lands: Solukhumbu and the upper Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi valleys of northeastern Nepal, from Solu to Helambu, and Kathmandu

facts.text: Sherpa communities use a customary system called nawa to look after crops and forests.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 90.3 percent of Sherpa people reported Sherpa as their own language.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Pangcah
nations.lands: East of the Central Mountain Range in Hualien and Taitung counties, plus the Hengchun Peninsula, Taiwan

facts.text: Their own name, Pangcah, means people and kinsmen. The name Amis came from neighbours in Taitung and was later adopted by scholars.
In some Pangcah communities, each age class takes its name from a key event of its time, so one class name marks the computer era.

nations.name: Karen
nations.lands: Eastern Myanmar, including Karen State, and western and northern Thailand

facts.text: Karen is a name for several related peoples who speak 12 related Karenic languages; about 85 percent of Karen belong to the S'gaw or Pwo branches.
Karen communities have lived in what is now northern Thailand for many centuries.

nations.name: Bodo
nations.lands: Bodoland Territorial Region and other parts of Assam, India

facts.text: Bodo is an associate official language of Assam, and in 2022 the state announced it would become a medium of instruction in Classes XI and XII.

source.title: CM Dr. Sarma attends 61st Annual conference of Bodo Sahitya Sabha (Press Release No. 129/2022)
source.publisher: Directorate of Information and Public Relations, Government of Assam

facts.text: Bodo is one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution.

source.title: Languages Included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
source.publisher: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, India

nations.name: Ibaloi
nations.lands: Southern Benguet and the Baguio area in northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Ibaloi are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Kankanaey and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry whose Ibaloi name is ayosip.

nations.name: Tripura
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts and other districts of Bangladesh, and the state of Tripura, India

facts.text: Tripura University opened a Department of Kokborok in 2015 and began doctoral research in the language in 2018.
Kokborok, the Tripura language, has been an official language of the Indian state of Tripura since 1979.

nations.name: Magar
nations.lands: Hills of the Rapti and Gandaki river basins in western and central Nepal, and communities across Nepal

facts.text: Magar communities keep customary institutions such as the bheja, and each year they choose a mukhiya as community leader, who settles small disputes.

source.title: मगर (Magar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Magar as an official language for both Gandaki and Karnali provinces.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tamu
nations.lands: Tamuwan, the hills between the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki rivers in central Nepal, including Gorkha, Lamjung, Kaski, Syangja, Manang and Mustang

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Gurung, the Tamu language, as an official language of Gandaki Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Tamu Kyui, the Tamu language, now has its own Khema script, which Nepal's Language Commission has recognized.

source.title: गुरुङ(तमू) (Gurung, Tamu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Kalasha
nations.lands: The Kalasha valleys of Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur in the Hindu Kush, Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

facts.text: Kalasha families use Suri Jagek to choose the right time to sow seeds and care for livestock, and to anticipate natural hazards.
Suri Jagek is practiced at local observatories in three Kalasha valley villages: Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur.

source.title: Pakistan's first independent nomination Suri Jagek inscribed by UNESCO (PR No. 04)
source.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan

nations.name: Sakizaya
nations.lands: Hualien Plain, the East Rift Valley and coast, Taiwan

facts.text: Through a cultural revival led by the community itself, the Sakizaya were recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2007.
The Sakizaya population was about 985 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kankanaey
nations.lands: Benguet and Mountain Province in the Cordillera of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Kankanaey are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Ibaloi and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry, known in Kankanaey as gotmo or alumani.

nations.name: Ifugao
nations.lands: Ifugao Province in the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: Ifugao families still farm and care for their mountain rice terraces, a UNESCO World Heritage living landscape since 1995.

source.title: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

facts.text: The Hudhud, long narrative chants of the Ifugao sung at rice sowing and harvest, are on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.

nations.name: Tao
nations.lands: Lanyu (Orchid Island), Taitung County, Taiwan

facts.text: The people call themselves Tao, meaning human, while Yami is the name used officially.
The Tao, who live on Lanyu, also called Orchid Island, numbered 4,684 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mizo
nations.lands: Mizoram, northeast India

facts.text: Mizoram became a full state of India on 20 February 1987; its Legislative Assembly first met on 10 May 1972.
Historically, every Mizo village had its own chief, who was assisted by a council of elders.

nations.name: Chakma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and parts of northeast India

facts.text: Hill Tracts peoples are sometimes called Jumma, after jum, their traditional method of shifting cultivation.
The Chakma make up more than half of the Indigenous population of Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Naga
nations.lands: Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh in India, and neighbouring Myanmar

facts.text: Nagaland's state portal lists 17 major tribes living in the state, each with its own language and festivals.

source.title: People and Culture
source.publisher: Nagaland State Portal, Government of Nagaland

facts.text: Each December the Government of Nagaland hosts the Hornbill Festival near Kohima, where all the state's tribes share their cultures.

nations.name: Newa
nations.lands: Swanigah, the Kathmandu Valley (Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur), and towns across Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Nepal Bhasa, alongside Tamang, as an official language of Bagmati Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Nepal Bhasa, the Newa language, has its own scripts, Ranjana and Prachalit, along with its own grammar, dictionaries and literature.

source.title: नेवार (Newar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Garo
nations.lands: Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, and north-central Bangladesh

facts.text: The Garo Hills Autonomous District Council, set up in 1952 under India's Sixth Schedule, is based in Tura and covers five districts.
The Meghalaya government lists Garo among the state's languages, alongside Khasi, Pnar and English.

nations.name: Orang Asli
nations.lands: Peninsular Malaysia

facts.text: Orang Asli, a Malay collective term meaning original or first peoples, covers 18 officially listed groups of Peninsular Malaysia.
Some Temuan, Jakun and Semai families now run their own rubber, oil palm or cocoa farms.

nations.name: Atayal
nations.lands: Mountain areas of northern and central Taiwan, across New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou and Yilan

facts.text: In the Atayal language, the word Atayal means people, real people, or kinspeople.
The Atayal live across the mountains of northern and central Taiwan, the widest spread of any Indigenous people on the island.

nations.name: Iban
nations.lands: Sarawak, Malaysia, with communities in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, and Brunei

facts.text: Between 1948 and 1963 the Iban language served as the common language between Sarawak's communities.

source.title: Indigenous peoples and ethnic minorities in Sarawak

facts.text: In 2011 the Tun Jugah Foundation published Bup Sereba Reti Jaku Iban, described as the first monolingual Iban dictionary.

nations.name: Mru
nations.lands: Bandarban district in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and nearby areas of Myanmar

facts.text: The Mru alphabet, invented in the 1980s and unrelated to any other script, is encoded in the Unicode Standard with its own digits.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: School textbooks up to class three have been published in the Mru language and alphabet.

nations.name: Kavalan
nations.lands: Yilan and the Hualien and Taitung coasts, Taiwan

facts.text: After a name rectification movement, the Kavalan were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2002.
The Kavalan population was about 1,492 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kadazandusun
nations.lands: Sabah, Malaysia

facts.text: The Kadazan Dusun Cultural Association, founded in 1966, represents 48 Indigenous ethnic communities of Sabah.
KDCA works on preserving, standardizing and developing the Kadazandusun language with its many dialects.

nations.name: Rapa Nui
nations.lands: Rapa Nui (Easter Island), in the south-eastern Pacific, Chile

facts.text: Tapati Rapa Nui, the island's main cultural festival, filled two weeks of February 2026 with ancestral competitions, arts and celebrations of Rapa Nui identity, language and traditions.

source.title: Ministra de las Culturas participa en inauguración de la Tapati Rapanui y desarrolla agenda de trabajo en la isla
source.publisher: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio (Chile)

facts.text: In 2017, 642 votes were cast in a formal consultation with the Rapa Nui people on a marine protected area for their island, and yes won all three questions.

source.title: Informe del Proceso de Consulta al pueblo Rapa Nui sobre creación, administración y regulación de usos de un Área Marina Costera Protegida de Múltiples Usos para Rapa Nui
source.publisher: Ministerio del Medio Ambiente, Gobierno de Chile

nations.name: Aṉangu
nations.lands: Central Australia, including Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa in the Northern Territory and the APY Lands of South Australia

facts.text: The park's board of management has 12 people, including eight Aboriginal members nominated by Traditional Owners.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

facts.text: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park was handed back to its Aṉangu Traditional Owners in 1985 and is jointly managed today.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

nations.name: Cook Islands Māori
nations.lands: the Cook Islands, including Rarotonga and the Southern and Northern Group islands

facts.text: Te Maeva Nui, held every early August, marks Cook Islands self-governance on 4 August and gathers communities from every island for song, dance, drumming and chant.
A 2003 law declared Cook Islands Māori an official language of the Cook Islands, alongside English, and set up a Māori language commission.

source.title: Te Reo Maori Act 2003 (Cook Islands)
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Yawuru
nations.lands: Broome (Rubibi) and the surrounding lands and seas, Kimberley, Western Australia, Australia

facts.text: Up to 1,500 children in Broome primary schools take part in Yawuru language programs.
In 2006 the Federal Court recognised Yawuru people as native title holders of about 530,000 hectares of country in and around Broome.

nations.name: Gunditjmara
nations.lands: South-west Victoria, including Budj Bim and Tae Rak (Lake Condah), Australia

facts.text: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation was set up in 2005 to continue Gunditjmara connection to country, including native title work.

source.title: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation | GMTOAC | 248 Condah Estate Road, Heywood VIC, Australia
source.publisher: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: All of the Budj Bim Cultural Landscape is Aboriginal owned or managed.

source.title: World heritage conservation of Budj Bim

nations.name: Te Arawa
nations.lands: Rotorua and the Rotorua lakes district, Bay of Plenty, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Rotorua was declared New Zealand's first bilingual district in 2017, and the council has since worked with Te Tatau o Te Arawa on changes like bilingual road signs.
The Te Arawa Lakes settlement, signed in 2004, provided for title to 13 lakebeds to be returned to Te Arawa, a large confederation of iwi and hapū.

source.title: Te Arawa Lakes
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Yapese
nations.lands: the main islands of Yap (Yap, Gagil, Tomil and Rumung) in Yap State, Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Yap's state constitution creates the Council of Pilung and the Council of Tamol, councils of traditional leaders whose work concerns tradition and custom.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Under Yap State law the two councils advise the Governor and Legislature and work to promote and preserve the traditions and customs of the people.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Tuvaluans
nations.lands: the nine islands of Tuvalu in the central Pacific, including Funafuti

facts.text: Each island in Tuvalu has a falekaupule, a traditional assembly of elders also called te sina o fenua, the grey-hairs of the land.

source.title: The Local Government System in Tuvalu

facts.text: Tuvaluan has eight dialects from eight of the islands, and the name Tuvalu joins tu, to stand, with valu, eight.

source.title: Tuvalu language activity book
source.publisher: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa

nations.name: Arrernte
nations.lands: Alice Springs and surrounding lands in Central Australia, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation, their native title body, looks after five Indigenous Land Use Agreements plus a land release agreement.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: Arrernte people from three estate groups, Antulye, Irlpme and Mparntwe, are the traditional owners of Alice Springs and its surrounding land.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: Tongans
nations.lands: the Kingdom of Tonga in the South Pacific, including Tongatapu, Vava'u, Ha'apai, 'Eua and the Niuas

facts.text: Tonga's 2021 census counted 100,179 people in the kingdom, a young population with a median age of 19 for males and 22 for females.
Lakalaka, often called Tonga's national dance, joins choreography, oratory and sung polyphony, and is performed at coronations and constitution anniversaries.

source.title: Lakalaka, dances and sung speeches of Tonga

nations.name: Tiwi
nations.lands: The Tiwi Islands (Bathurst and Melville Islands), about 80 km north of Darwin in the Arafura Sea, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: There are eight landowning groups on the Tiwi Islands, and Tiwi people have an unbroken history of occupying and owning their islands.
The Tiwi Islands, about 80 km north of Darwin, are home to just over 3,000 people, more than 90 percent of them Tiwi.

nations.name: Gamilaraay
nations.lands: North-central New South Wales into southern Queensland, Australia

facts.text: The Australian National University teaches Gamilaraay as a heritage language that its custodians are actively reviving.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

facts.text: Student work in the ANU Gamilaraay course feeds into materials for Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay language revival, taught with a free textbook called Wiidhaa.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

nations.name: Ngāti Porou
nations.lands: Te Tairāwhiti, the East Coast of the North Island, from Pōtikirua to Te Toka-a-Taiau, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Porou's tribal area runs down Te Tairāwhiti, between Pōtikirua (Lottin Point) in the north and Te Toka-a-Taiau in the south.
The Ngāti Porou pepeha names Hikurangi as their mountain and Waiapu as their river.

nations.name: ni-Vanuatu
nations.lands: the islands of the Republic of Vanuatu in the south-west Pacific, including Malakula and the central and northern islands

facts.text: Vanuatu Cultural Centre fieldworkers, or filwokas, are volunteers nominated by their communities across the islands to promote, protect and preserve kastom.

source.title: Grassroots Badly Burnt: the loss of ni-Vanuatu archaeologists whose careers spanned 50 years

facts.text: In 1998 Na'hai speakers of south Malakula opened the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta, the first language-based cultural centre in Vanuatu.

source.title: Kastom as Development: Opening the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta

nations.name: Meriam
nations.lands: Mer (Murray Island) and nearby islands in the eastern Torres Strait, Queensland, Australia

facts.text: Meriam Mir is the traditional language of Mer, an island in the far east of the Torres Strait from which the Great Barrier Reef can be seen.

source.title: Murray Island - Mer Eruer Uteb
source.publisher: Tagai State College (Queensland Department of Education)

nations.name: Rotumans
nations.lands: the island of Rotuma and its islets, about 500 km north of Fiji's main islands, and communities across Fiji

facts.text: Rotuma is divided into seven districts, each led by a district chief, the gagaj 'es itu'u, with village groups called ho'aga under their own chiefs.

source.title: Hierarchy (Kato'aga: Rotuman Ceremonies)
source.publisher: The Rotuma Website, University of Hawai'i

facts.text: Rotumans are a distinct people with their own language, Fäeag Rotuạm, which New Zealand celebrates each year in Rotuman Language Week.

source.title: Gasav Ne Fäeag Rotuạm Ta: Rotuman Language Week

nations.name: Kanak
nations.lands: New Caledonia, including Grande Terre and the Loyalty Islands

facts.text: Since 2016 every pupil in New Caledonia must be taught the fundamentals of Kanak culture, and every school must offer teaching in Kanak languages.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

facts.text: Kanak society is organised by custom: clans join into tribes within customary districts, which are grouped into eight customary areas.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

nations.name: Ngāi Tūhoe
nations.lands: Te Urewera, in the eastern North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: A Treaty settlement signed in 2013 provided for Te Urewera, the Tūhoe homeland, to have its own law and a separate legal identity, governed by Tūhoe and Crown nominees.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

facts.text: Tūhoe had about 9,300 registered members at the time of their 2013 Treaty settlement.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Tokelauans
nations.lands: the three atolls of Tokelau, Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo, in the South Pacific

facts.text: In Tokelau the Taupulega, the village councils of elders, remain the ultimate source of authority, and they grant the General Fono its powers.
The role of Ulu-o-Tokelau, head of the national government, rotates each year among the elected leaders of Tokelau's three atolls.

nations.name: I-Kiribati
nations.lands: the Republic of Kiribati in the central Pacific, across the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands

facts.text: In Kiribati the mwaneaba, the traditional meeting house, is where village decisions are made by the unimwane, the senior men, whose seating shows their standing.

source.title: Te Mwaneaba ni Kiribati: The Traditional Meeting House of Kiribati
source.publisher: Shima: The International Journal of Research into Island Cultures

facts.text: In 2010 the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, about 408,250 square kilometres of ocean and islands, became the first World Heritage site in Kiribati.

nations.name: Wiradjuri
nations.lands: Central New South Wales, the country of the Wambool (Macquarie), Kalari (Lachlan) and Murrumbidjeri (Murrumbidgee) rivers, Australia

facts.text: A Charles Sturt University course shaped by Wiradjuri Elders works to build a living community of Wiradjuri speakers; it won a 2019 MacJannet Prize.

source.title: The Graduate Certificate in Wiradjuri Language Culture and Heritage, Charles Sturt University (Australia)
source.publisher: Talloires Network of Engaged Universities (Tufts University)

facts.text: Wiradjuri country covers a large part of New South Wales, reaching out from the Great Dividing Range.

nations.name: Papuan peoples
nations.lands: The Papua region of Indonesia, the western half of the island of New Guinea

facts.text: Men and women in Papua use the noken to carry garden produce, and it may also be worn at festivities or given as a peace offering.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

facts.text: The noken, a bag that communities in Papua knot or weave by hand from wood fibre or leaves, was inscribed on a UNESCO list for urgent safeguarding in 2012.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

nations.name: Mā'ohi
nations.lands: French Polynesia, including Tahiti and the other islands of its five archipelagos

facts.text: A new website interface announced in 2017 by the Tahitian Academy, Fare Vāna'a, adds French to Tahitian search to its Tahitian to French dictionary.

source.title: Evolution du site internet du Fare Vāna’a & application
source.publisher: Service public de la Polynésie française (DGEN)

facts.text: UNESCO honours mā'ohi skill in sailing outrigger canoes across long stretches of ocean, navigating by observing natural phenomena.

nations.name: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
also: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Wewoka and Seminole County, Oklahoma, United States; earlier homelands in Florida

facts.text: The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is made up of fourteen bands, and its General Council seats two representatives from each band rather than from districts.

source.title: The Great Seminole Nation of Oklahoma: Written Testimony to the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs
source.publisher: Seminole Nation of Oklahoma, via U.S. Senate Committee on Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Seminole Nation Language Program works to maintain, revitalize and carry forward the language and traditional ways of the Seminole people.

nations.name: Rappahannock Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds in Virginia, as described by the Tribe's environmental department

facts.text: The Tribe's environmental department says it coordinates the Return to the River youth program.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe dates its incorporation to 1921 as part of efforts to strengthen its government and seek recognition.

nations.name: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation
nations.lands: Guntersville, Alabama

facts.text: A January 2020 post describes a Word of the Month practice series, with a new calendar of practice planned for February.
In January 2020, the Nation announced a plan to highlight enrolled citizens' crafted items in its public posts.

source.title: Attention: United Cherokee AniYunWiYa Nation Artisans - UCAN

nations.name: Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe
nations.lands: Akwesasne, on the St. Lawrence River in northern New York, United States; the wider Akwesasne community extends into Canada

facts.text: The Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Council is made up of three Chiefs, three Sub-Chiefs and a Tribal Clerk, with elections scheduled each year and set terms of office.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

facts.text: The Tribe describes its original homeland as northeastern New York State, reaching into southern Canada and Vermont.

source.title: History of Tribal Government | SRMT - NSN

nations.name: Coharie Tribe
nations.lands: Harnett and Sampson Counties in southeastern North Carolina, where the Tribe locates its present community

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council as representing Harnett and Sampson Counties.
The Tribe's history locates the present Coharie population in North Carolina's Harnett and Sampson Counties.

nations.name: Seneca Nation
nations.lands: Allegany, Cattaraugus and Oil Spring territories in Western New York, United States

facts.text: The Seneca Nation governs itself under a constitution established in 1848, with a 16-member Tribal Council drawn equally from the Cattaraugus and Allegany territories.

source.title: Seneca Nation of Indians - Official Website

facts.text: The Seneca Nation runs a language immersion program so students can hold conversations in Onöndowa’ga:’ Gawë:nö’, the Seneca language, alongside classes and online learning.

nations.name: Cherokee Nation
nations.lands: Tahlequah and a 14-county reservation area in Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in the Southeast

facts.text: Cherokee Nation governs through legislative, executive and judicial branches and serves people across a 14-county reservation area.
Written Cherokee uses a syllabary, not an alphabet, with 85 distinct characters; Cherokee Nation teaches it through an immersion school and a master-apprentice program.

nations.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
nations.lands: The Qualla Boundary in western North Carolina, United States, beside the Great Smoky Mountains

facts.text: As a sovereign nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its own laws, holds its own elections and runs its own government and institutions.

source.title: Home - Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians

facts.text: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its home on the 56,000-acre Qualla Boundary, next to Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

source.title: NC Tribal Communities | NC DOA
source.publisher: North Carolina Department of Administration, Commission of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Seminole Tribe of Florida
nations.lands: Big Cypress, Brighton, Fort Pierce, Hollywood, Immokalee and Tampa reservations in Florida, United States

facts.text: The Tribal Council, with a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and representatives from each reservation, is the chief governing body of the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
Adding the Tampa and Immokalee reservations brought the Seminole Tribe of Florida's federal trust lands to more than 90,000 acres.

nations.name: Southeastern Mvskoke Nation
nations.lands: Near Troy in Alabama; its history describes organization around Pike and Coffee Counties.

facts.text: The Nation presents its language page as a small learning resource for Tribal members and other Mvskokes.
Its introduction locates the Nation near Troy in Alabama.

nations.name: Delaware Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Bartlesville, Oklahoma, United States; homelands along the Delaware River

facts.text: The Delaware Tribe of Indians is a federally recognized tribe of the Lenape people, headquartered in Bartlesville, Oklahoma.
The Tribe's online Lenape Talking Dictionary holds about 15,380 words, along with recorded stories and songs, and is still growing.

source.title: Language Revitalization - Delaware Tribe of Indians

pronounce.publisher: Delaware Tribe of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana
nations.lands: Southwest Louisiana; the Tribe describes a community centered in Allen Parish

facts.text: The Tribe dates its first Tribal Council elections to 1985 and describes staggered four-year terms.
The Tribe describes a five-member elected council: four council members and a chairman.

nations.name: Passamaquoddy (Peskotomuhkati)
nations.lands: Sipayik (Pleasant Point) and Motahkomikuk (Indian Township) in Maine, United States, and a community in New Brunswick, Canada

facts.text: Over 3,000 Passamaquoddy citizens belong to three self-governing communities, two in Maine and one in New Brunswick, linked by political, cultural and kinship ties.
The Maliseet-Passamaquoddy Dictionary has more than 19,000 entries, and many older tribal members still speak the language fluently.

nations.name: MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama, near the Mobile and Tombigbee Rivers

facts.text: The Tribe's introduction places its communities in Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama.
Its history dates an effort to obtain federal aid for Alabama Choctaw schools to 1934.

source.title: Social Barriers - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Choctaw communities in east-central Mississippi, United States

facts.text: In 1945 the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians ratified a Constitution that authorized the Tribe's separation from the state of Mississippi.

source.title: About Us - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.text: The Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians has more than 11,000 tribal members.

source.title: Home Page - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Durant and a reservation of eight whole and five partial counties in southeastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi

facts.text: Chahta Anumpa Aiikhvna, the School of Choctaw Language, offers classes for every skill level plus a Speak Choctaw app.
The Choctaw Nation reservation covers 10,864 square miles in southeastern Oklahoma, taking in eight whole counties and parts of five more.

nations.name: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southampton County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is based in Southampton County, Virginia.
The Tribe's language page publishes a vocabulary drawn from materials dating to March 4, 1820.

nations.name: Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas
nations.lands: East Texas; the Tribe describes its reservation in the Big Thicket

facts.text: The Tribe's government page states that its elected Tribal Council members serve three-year terms.
The Tribe describes an elected Tribal Council advised by its Chiefs. The profile concerns this Texas Tribal government, not every Alabama or Coushatta community.

nations.name: Shinnecock Indian Nation
nations.lands: In and around the Town of Southampton on the eastern end of Long Island, New York, United States

facts.text: On October 1, 2010, the Shinnecock Indian Nation was formally recognized by the United States as the 565th federally recognized tribe.
The Shinnecock Indian Nation has over 1,589 enrolled tribal members.

nations.name: Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia
nations.lands: southeastern Virginia along the Nottoway River; the Tribe's Community House & Interpretive Center is in Capron

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes the Nottoway as Iroquoian speakers of southeastern Virginia.

source.title: Tribal History - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

facts.text: The Tribe says its Community House & Interpretive Center formally opened in Capron on May 5, 2012.

source.title: Community House & Interpretive Center - Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

nations.name: Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
nations.lands: Along the Lumbee River in Robeson, Hoke, Cumberland and Scotland counties, North Carolina, United States, centered on Pembroke

facts.text: The Lumbee Tribe became fully federally recognized by the United States on December 18, 2025.
The Lumbee Tribe describes its people, the People of the Dark Water, as entrepreneurial and strongly focused on education.

nations.name: Oneida Indian Nation
nations.lands: Central New York, United States

facts.text: Oneida Indian Nation Members learn Onyota’a:ká:, the Oneida language, through intensive courses, a preschool curriculum, e-books, smartphone apps and an Oneida language keyboard.
During the American Revolution, Oneidas fought alongside the colonists and carried corn to feed General Washington's starving soldiers; the Nation honors them as America's first allies.

nations.name: Imazighen
nations.lands: North Africa (Tamazgha): Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt's Siwa oasis, with communities across the Sahel and in the diaspora

facts.text: After decades of campaigning, Tamazight was recognized as a national and official language in Algeria's Constitution in 2016.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Algeria
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Amazigh identity and the Amazigh language, Tamazight, have had official recognition in Morocco's Constitution since 2011.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Morocco
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Griqua
nations.lands: the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa

facts.text: Griqua communities live today in the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Early Griqua communities governed themselves through leaders called kaptyns, with magistrates drawn from leading families.

nations.name: Siwans
nations.lands: the oases of Siwa and El-Gara in Egypt's Western Desert, near the border with Libya

facts.text: A sense of Berber belonging has revived in Siwa this century; a letter of the Tifinagh alphabet, the Amazigh symbol, now names a bazaar below old Shali.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

facts.text: Ten Siwan tribes speak Siwi, an eastern Amazigh (Berber) language, in the oases of Siwa and El-Gara.

source.title: Siwa, the Berber oasis where cultures cross (An Atlas of Contemporary Egypt, 2023)

nations.name: Khwe
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia, north-western Botswana and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, Khwe and !Xun communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Khwe people in Namibia have their own Traditional Authority. As of 2025 the government had not recognized it, which Khwe say makes land and development issues harder to resolve.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ogiek
nations.lands: highland forests of Kenya, especially the Mau Forest

facts.text: In December 2025 the African Court issued its first ever compliance decision, in the Ogiek case, finding that Kenya had not yet carried out its judgments.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Kenya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2017 the African Court ruled for the Ogiek, its first ruling for an Indigenous people, and recognized Indigenous peoples as guardians of local ecosystems.

nations.name: Datooga
nations.lands: northern Tanzania, including the highlands near Mount Hanang in Manyara Region and the Lake Eyasi area

facts.text: Datooga and Hadza communities own more than 110,000 hectares of dryland forest protected through the Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape project.
With help from the NGO Ujamaa Community Resource Team, Barabaig communities in northern Tanzania gained grazing land held under collective title.

nations.name: Hai//om
nations.lands: north-central Namibia, in and around Etosha National Park and on resettlement farms in Kunene, Oshikoto and Oshana regions

facts.text: In July 2026 Namibia's Vice President opened a high-level meeting in Outjo with the Hai//om Traditional Authority on a development plan for Hai//om communities.

source.title: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Hai-//om Community Development, Vice President Lucia Witbooi (speech)

facts.text: Many Hai//om communities lived on lands that are now Etosha National Park and the surrounding regions, according to the Hai//om Community San Council.

source.title: Challenges Faced by the Hai//om San Marginalized Communities in Namibia: Challenges and Solutions
source.publisher: Cultural Survival (by the Hai//om Community San Council)

nations.name: Wodaabe
nations.lands: the Sahel of Niger, with communities in Chad, northern Cameroon and north-east Nigeria

facts.text: In 2008 thousands of Wodaabe herders attended the fourth General Assembly of the Woodaabe Pastoralists of Niger.

source.title: Oromo pastoralists visit Woodaabe General Assembly in Niger

facts.text: Cattle herding is the main livelihood of the Wodaabe, who move with the seasons across the Sahel.

nations.name: Konso
nations.lands: the Konso highlands of south-western Ethiopia

facts.text: The Konso built the dry-stone terraces of their highlands and still farm them; UNESCO lists the Konso Cultural Landscape as World Heritage.
The Konso raise stone steles to mark the handing of responsibility from the older generation to the younger, a living tradition.

nations.name: Kel Tamasheq
nations.lands: the Sahara and Sahel: northern Mali and Niger, southern Algeria and Libya, and northern Burkina Faso

facts.text: In Libya, the Fezzan region, including Ubari and Ghat, is traditional Kel Tamasheq territory, linked to communities across the borders in Niger and Algeria.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Libya
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In Niger, Kel Tamasheq (Tuareg) herders raise camels and goats in Agadez, Tahoua and Tillabéry. Estimates for 2009 put them at about 1.2 million, 8.3% of the population.

source.title: Indigenous World 2020: Niger
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Endorois
nations.lands: around Lake Bogoria in Baringo County, and in Nakuru and Laikipia counties, in Kenya's Rift Valley

facts.text: The Endorois Welfare Council, founded in 1995 by senior members of the community, works for justice and sustainable development for the Endorois.

source.title: Endorois Welfare Council - Endorois Welfare Council for marginalized communities

facts.text: In 2010 the African Union approved an African Commission ruling in the Endorois case, the first in Africa to recognize Indigenous peoples' rights to land they traditionally owned.

source.title: Landmark decision rules Kenya’s removal of indigenous people from ancestral land illegal

nations.name: Yiaku
nations.lands: Mukogodo Forest in Laikipia County, Kenya

facts.text: Yiaku women and elders now lead language teaching and forest care, and growing youth involvement is strengthening the community.

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship
source.publisher: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)

facts.text: Since 2003 the Yiaku Laikipiak Trust has worked to protect Mukogodo Forest and keep Yiaku culture alive.

source.title: Reviving Indigenous forest stewardship
source.publisher: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)

nations.name: Anywaa
nations.lands: Gambella in western Ethiopia, along the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers, and neighbouring South Sudan

facts.text: Anywaa activists helped found EMIPRO in 2022, the first legally registered Indigenous-led rights organization in Ethiopia.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

facts.text: The Anywaa are river farmers and fishers whose lives follow the Akobo, Alwaro, Openo (Baro) and Gilo rivers of Gambella.

source.title: “We Belong to This Land:” The Anywaa Peoples’ Fight for Survival, Dignity, and Recognition in Ethiopia

nations.name: Toubou
nations.lands: the Tibesti plateau of northern Chad, southern Libya along the Chad border, and northern Niger

facts.text: Toubou herders practise mobile pastoralism across a wide area stretching from northern Niger to Sudan.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Libya chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: About 50,000 Toubou live in Libya along the border with Chad; the people's origins lie in the Tibesti plateau.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Libya chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Rifians
nations.lands: the Rif of northern and north-eastern Morocco, including Al Hoceima province

facts.text: In Morocco's 2024 census, 53.6% of people in Al Hoceima province said they use Tarifit, the language of the Irifiyen.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima

facts.text: Nationwide, 3.2% of Morocco's population reported Tarifit among the local languages they use, in the 2024 census.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima

nations.name: Baka
nations.lands: forests of eastern and southern Cameroon, northern Gabon, and neighbouring parts of the Republic of the Congo and Central African Republic

facts.text: In Gabon, the Baka are one of nine Indigenous forest peoples, alongside the Babongo, Bakoya and others, each with its own language and culture.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Gabon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2025 a Batouri workshop run by the association ASBABUK and Cameroon's forestry ministry focused on fully recognizing Baka as rightful partners in managing forest resources.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Sengwer
nations.lands: Cherangany Hills and Embobut Forest in Kenya's western highlands

facts.text: Sengwer society is organized around clans, each with its own roles, and elders guide decisions and teach younger generations.
Sengwer knowledge includes sustainable ways of hunting, gathering, beekeeping and caring for forest resources, which helps conserve biodiversity.

nations.name: Kabyles
nations.lands: Kabylia in north-eastern Algeria, with a large community in France

facts.text: Taqbaylit, the Kabyle language, is one of three Amazigh languages taught from bachelor's level to doctorate at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

facts.text: Kabyles make up around half of Algeria's Amazigh population, centred on Kabylia in the north-east.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Algeria chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mozabite
nations.lands: the M'Zab valley around Ghardaïa in the Algerian Sahara

facts.text: UNESCO credits the M'Zab with an ingenious system for capturing and sharing water which, with its palm groves, makes life work in a semi-desert.
The M'Zab valley habitat, built in the tenth century by the Ibadites around five ksour (fortified towns), survives intact and is UNESCO World Heritage.

nations.name: BaAka
nations.lands: forests between the Oubangui and Sangha rivers, in south-western Central African Republic and northern Republic of the Congo

facts.text: Dzanga-Sangha Protected Areas credits BaAka knowledge of the forest as central to its research, conservation and tourism work.
The Central African Republic, home to many BaAka communities, ratified ILO Convention 169 on Indigenous peoples in 2010, the first African state to do so.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2021: Central African Republic
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
nations.lands: Northern Cheyenne Reservation, southeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Lame Deer

facts.text: Lame Deer, Montana, is home to the Northern Cheyenne tribal government headquarters, and the Tribal Council is elected by district.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: About 99 percent of the Northern Cheyenne Reservation, roughly 444,000 acres in southeastern Montana, is owned by the tribe.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Comanche Nation
nations.lands: Southwest Oklahoma, United States; headquarters north of Lawton

facts.text: The Comanche Nation's main governing body is its Tribal Council, made up of every enrolled member over age 18.
The Comanche Nation language program works to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche language, including through online learning.

pronounce.text: Nʉmʉnʉʉ, the Comanche name for the people: NUH-MUH-NUH
pronounce.publisher: Comanche Nation, on its own site

nations.name: Apsáalooke Nation
nations.lands: Crow Indian Reservation, south-central Montana, United States; headquarters at Crow Agency

facts.text: The Apsáalooke Nation's government has three branches: executive, legislative and judicial.

source.title: Official Site of the Crow Tribe Executive Branch - Home

facts.text: Montana's state tribal directory reports that most Apsáalooke people speak Crow as their first language.

source.title: Crow Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Spirit Lake Nation
nations.lands: Northeastern North Dakota, mainly Benson County, United States; headquarters at Fort Totten

facts.text: Cankdeska Cikana Community College, the tribal college at Spirit Lake, offers 12 associate degree and certificate programs.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

facts.text: At Spirit Lake both English and the Dakota language are spoken, specifically the Eastern Dakota dialect.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Fort Sill Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma; reservation land in New Mexico, United States

facts.text: The Fort Sill Apache Tribe comprises descendants of Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches displaced from the Southwest and northern Mexico.
The General Council, made up of adult tribal members, elects the Business Committee and approves the tribal operations budget.

nations.name: Oneida Nation
also: Oneida Tribe of Indians of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Oneida Reservation, Brown and Outagamie counties, northeast Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Oneida Nation is governed by an elected Business Committee of nine members, which makes decisions by majority rule.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

facts.text: The Oneida Reservation lies in Brown and Outagamie counties in northeast Wisconsin.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma; the Tribe publishes its offices in Ponca City

facts.text: The Tribe lists preparing an annual funding agreement for Tribal Council review and approval among its self-governance office's duties.

source.title: Self-Governance
source.publisher: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

facts.text: The Tribe describes preservation work that includes Section 106 reviews and consultation with federal, Tribal, state and local agencies.

source.title: Historic Preservation
source.publisher: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

nations.name: Citizen Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Headquartered in Shawnee, Oklahoma, United States, with citizens around the world

facts.text: In July 2026 the Citizen Potawatomi Nation signed the articles of confederation for the Potawatomi Confederacy.
The Citizen Potawatomi Nation Constitution dates from 1938 and was amended in 1985 and again in 2007.

nations.name: Kaw Nation
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with historical homelands in Kansas and the Great Plains

facts.text: The Nation's history distinguishes a Tribal Council from a General Council composed of enrolled adult citizens.
The Nation's language page lists online learning and a basic Kanza course. Listed materials remain under the publisher's access and use conditions.

nations.name: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate
nations.lands: Lake Traverse Reservation, northeastern South Dakota and southeastern North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The Lake Traverse Reservation reaches across seven counties, five in South Dakota and two in North Dakota.
The Oyate counts more than 14,000 tribal members, living across the United States and serving abroad in the Armed Forces.

nations.name: Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes
nations.lands: Western Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Concho

facts.text: The Cheyenne and Arapaho Language Program offers classes in tribal communities and online for tribal members.

source.title: Language and Culture | Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

facts.text: The tribes run adult immersion training aimed at producing functionally fluent speakers of both the Cheyenne and Arapaho languages.

source.title: Language and Culture | Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes

nations.name: Meskwaki Nation
also: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa
nations.lands: Meskwaki Settlement near Tama, Iowa, United States

facts.text: The Meskwaki Nation has its own constitution, codified laws, police officers and a fully functioning court system.

source.title: History | Meskwaki | Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi
source.publisher: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

facts.text: The Meskwaki language is close to the Sauk and Kickapoo dialects, and the people are working hard to keep it strong.

source.title: History | Meskwaki | Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi
source.publisher: Sac & Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa

nations.name: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community
nations.lands: Scott County, Minnesota, United States

facts.text: Following the Dakota tradition of helping others, the SMSC gives millions of dollars each year to other tribes, organizations and local governments.

source.title: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community in Scott County, MN

facts.text: The community says plainly that it is still here, living traditional Dakota lifeways that will pass on to future generations.

source.title: Our History - Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community in Scott County, MN

nations.name: Caddo Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with offices in Binger; the Nation describes ancestral homelands in present-day Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas

facts.text: The Nation's Historic Preservation Department describes work in repatriation and consultation, and publishes separate procedures for Section 106 and NAGPRA requests.
The Nation dates the beginning of its current language program to August 1, 2022. This institutional milestone does not date the start of Caddo language preservation.

nations.name: Oglala Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Pine Ridge Reservation, southwestern South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The Pine Ridge Reservation, home of the Oglala Sioux Tribe, covers about 2.1 million acres across Oglala Lakota, Jackson and Bennett counties in South Dakota.

source.title: Pine Ridge Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Bureau of Indian Affairs estimates enrollment in the Oglala Sioux Tribe at 46,855 members.

source.title: Pine Ridge Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Omaha Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Omaha Reservation, Nebraska, United States; tribal offices in Macy

facts.text: The Omaha Tribe of Nebraska holds a trust land base of 27,828 acres, according to the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

source.title: Winnebago Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Bureau of Indian Affairs estimates enrollment in the Omaha Tribe of Nebraska at 5,427 members.

source.title: Winnebago Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe
nations.lands: Three districts in East Central Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Mille Lacs Band governs itself through a three-branch government that divides power among executive, legislative and judicial branches.

source.title: Welcome | Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe

facts.text: The Mille Lacs Band is a self-governing nation of nearly 4,800 enrolled members, with homelands in three districts of East Central Minnesota.

source.title: Welcome | Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe

nations.name: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Rolette County, North Dakota, near the Canadian border, United States

facts.text: Members of the Turtle Mountain Band speak English, Ojibwe and Michif, a language that blends French, Ojibwe and Cree.

source.title: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

facts.text: As of July 2024, an estimated 33,276 members were enrolled in the Turtle Mountain Band.

source.title: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nations.lands: central Oklahoma, including the Shawnee and Little Axe areas

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes separate Legislative/Executive and Judicial branches, alongside an independent Election Commission.

source.title: Government | Absentee Shawnee Tribe
source.publisher: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

facts.text: The Tribe's language page lists a lexicon and online lessons among its resources; the index does not establish access conditions or teaching availability.

source.title: Language | Absentee Shawnee Tribe
source.publisher: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma

nations.name: Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Eastern Upper Peninsula of Michigan, United States

facts.text: Sault Tribe serves seven eastern Upper Peninsula counties: Chippewa, Luce, Mackinac, Schoolcraft, Alger, Delta and Marquette.

source.title: About Us - The Sault Tribe of Chippewa Indians Official Web Site
source.publisher: Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: Sault Tribe is a federally recognized tribe of about 44,000 members.

source.title: About Us - The Sault Tribe of Chippewa Indians Official Web Site
source.publisher: Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians

nations.name: Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; centered in Perkins

facts.text: The Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma is a sovereign nation centered in Perkins, Oklahoma, with self-government recognized by treaties and legislation.
The Iowa people's own name, Baxoje, means People of the Grey Snow.

pronounce.text: Baxoje, the people's own name: Bah Kho-je
pronounce.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma, on its own site

nations.name: Syilx Okanagan Nation
nations.lands: The Okanagan, Similkameen and Nicola areas of British Columbia, Canada, and northern Washington State, United States

facts.text: Historically the Okanagan Nation Alliance represented eight member communities: seven in Canada and the Colville Confederated Tribes in Washington State.
The Okanagan Nation Alliance reports that the new Okanagan Dam Fish Passage, after years of advocacy and planning, lets salmon reach Okanagan Lake for the first time in nearly 100 years.

nations.name: Kahnawà:ke
nations.lands: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence River, near Montreal, Quebec, Canada

facts.text: For more than a hundred years, many people from Kahnawà:ke, mostly men, have worked in the ironworking trade, much of it in the United States.
About 8,000 people live in Kahnawà:ke, on the banks of the St. Lawrence River about 10 kilometres south of Montreal.

nations.name: Nunavik Inuit
nations.lands: Nunavik, northern Quebec, Canada: 15 villages along Hudson Bay, Hudson Strait and Ungava Bay

facts.text: Makivvik, an Inuktitut name meaning 'to rise up', protects Nunavik Inuit rights under the 1975 James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement, Canada's first comprehensive Inuit land claim.
Language retention among Nunavik Inuit is over 95 percent, and Inuktitut remains the main language spoken in the region.

nations.name: Inuit of Nunavut
nations.lands: Nunavut, Canada: the Qikiqtaaluk, Kivalliq and Kitikmeot regions

facts.text: Nunavut became Canada's newest territory on April 1, 1999, and Inuktitut is an official language of its government with Inuinnaqtun, English and French.
Under the agreement Inuit own about 350,000 square kilometres of land, including about 35,000 square kilometres with mineral rights.

nations.name: Wolastoqiyik
nations.lands: The Wolastoq (Saint John River) watershed, from the Bay of Fundy to the St. Lawrence: New Brunswick and Quebec in Canada, and Maine in the United States

facts.text: Six Wolastoqey communities in New Brunswick, Matawaskiye, Neqotkuk, Pilick, Sitansisk, Welamukotuk and Wotstak, work together through the Wolastoqey Nation in New Brunswick.
The Wolastoqiyik are the people of the Wolastoq watershed, a homeland of land, sea and fresh water reaching from the Bay of Fundy to the St. Lawrence River.

nations.name: Siksika Nation
nations.lands: East of Calgary, Alberta, Canada; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: Siksika's coat of arms, registered with the Canadian Heraldic Authority in June 1992, was the first registered by any Nation in Canada.
Siksika Nation has about 7,800 members, and its language is Siksika, or Blackfoot.

nations.name: Nuu-chah-nulth
nations.lands: The west coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council serves fourteen Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations with about 10,000 members, grouped in three regions.
The Council's vision is self-government that builds strong, healthy Nuu-chah-nulth communities.

nations.name: Inuit
nations.lands: Inuit Nunangat: the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Nunavut, Nunavik and Nunatsiavut in Arctic Canada

facts.text: Roughly 60 percent of Inuit can hold a conversation in Inuktut, the Inuit language.
Most Inuit in Canada live in 51 communities across Inuit Nunangat, a homeland covering about 40 percent of Canada's land and 72 percent of its coastline.

nations.name: xʷməθkʷəy̓əm
nations.lands: The Fraser River estuary, including much of Metro Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Musqueam is a strong, growing community of more than 1,300 members, many living on the Musqueam reserve near the mouth of the Fraser River.
The name xʷməθkʷəy̓əm means place of the məθkʷəy̓, a plant, and Musqueam people are traditionally hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ speakers.

nations.name: Inuvialuit
nations.lands: The Inuvialuit Settlement Region in the western Arctic, Northwest Territories and Yukon, Canada

facts.text: Six communities lie within the Inuvialuit Settlement Region: Aklavik, Inuvik, Paulatuk, Sachs Harbour, Tuktoyaktuk and Ulukhaktok.
One of the agreement's basic goals is keeping Inuvialuit cultural identity and values strong as northern society changes.

nations.name: Kainai
nations.lands: Southern Alberta, Canada, with its main community at Standoff; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: The Blood Tribe's stated mission is to preserve and protect its lands, culture, language and traditions in the spirit of Kainayssini.
In 2026 the Blood Tribe Land Management Department won a Prairie Conservation Award.

nations.name: Eeyou
also: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee)
nations.lands: Eeyou Istchee, the lands east of James Bay and Hudson Bay in northern Quebec, Canada

facts.text: Each Eeyou First Nation runs its own local government, and every elected Chief also sits on the board of the Grand Council of the Crees to address shared issues.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

facts.text: Eeyou Istchee is home to more than 20,000 people.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

nations.name: Nation Wendat
nations.lands: Wendake, near Québec City, within the traditional territory Onyionhwentsïio’ in Quebec, Canada

facts.text: After the Wendat language went dormant in the 1800s, the Yawenda project (2007 to 2012) brought language specialists and community members together to revive it.
The Nation counts more than 300 Wendat businesses, including many artisans, artists and cultural organizations.

nations.name: səlilwətaɬ
nations.lands: Burrard Inlet (səlilwət) in North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Tsleil-Waututh people see caring for the lands and waters of their territory as a birthright and obligation, so future generations can thrive.
Tsleil-Waututh means 'People of the Inlet'. The Nation's language is hən̓q̓əmin̓əm, in which its name is səlilwətaɬ.

nations.name: Akwesasne
nations.lands: Along the St. Lawrence River where Ontario, Quebec and New York State meet, in Canada and the United States

facts.text: Akwesasne spans lands in Quebec, Ontario and New York State, and three separate but linked political bodies govern it.
Kanien'kéha, the Mohawk language, remains central to identity in Akwesasne and is actively taught in its schools.

nations.name: Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw
nations.lands: The North Shore of Vancouver and the Squamish River valley, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nation's roots lie in several communities that became one government in 1923. Most members live on Vancouver's North Shore, others along the Squamish River.
The Squamish language is a sign of resilience: dozens of Nation members are learning it from their Elders as a second language.

nations.name: Haida Nation
nations.lands: Haida Gwaii, an archipelago off the north coast of British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Council of the Haida Nation works to steward the lands and waters of Haida territories and carry Haida culture and language to future generations.
In April 2024 British Columbia and the Council of the Haida Nation signed the Rising Tide agreement, a first of its kind recognizing Haida Aboriginal title in Haida Gwaii.

source.title: For Immediate Release: Haida Nation, B.C. recognize Haida Aboriginal title, a historic first in Canada

nations.name: Mescalero Apache
nations.lands: South-central New Mexico, US (Mescalero Apache Reservation)

facts.text: Today three peoples, the Mescalero, Lipan and Chiricahua Apache, together make up the Mescalero Apache Tribe on a 463,000 acre reservation.
The Mescalero Apache Tribe owns and runs the Inn of the Mountain Gods Resort and the Ski Apache ski area.

source.title: Official Website of the Mescalero Apache Tribe

nations.name: Jicarilla Apache
nations.lands: North-central New Mexico, US, along the Colorado line and across the Continental Divide (Dulce)

facts.text: The Jicarilla Apache Nation reservation spans more than 879,917 acres in north-central New Mexico, and Dulce is its only community and tribal headquarters.
After 1887 the Jicarilla moved their individual allotments back into tribal ownership, keeping their lands and water rights together.

nations.name: Akimel O’otham
nations.lands: Gila River Indian Community, south of Phoenix, Arizona, US, shared with the Pee Posh (Maricopa)

facts.text: The Akimel O’otham welcomed the Pee Posh (Maricopa) to the Gila River long ago, and the two peoples still share its lands and resources today.
Akimel O’otham basket weaving is in revival, and in 2004 the community dedicated the Huhugam Heritage Center to care for its heritage.

nations.name: Yoreme
nations.lands: Southern Sonora (Etchojoa, Huatabampo, Navojoa) and northern Sinaloa (Ahome, El Fuerte, Guasave), Mexico

facts.text: Yoreme communities have traditional governors. In December 2025 they met Mexico’s federal agrarian office to set a path for continuing the Yoreme-Mayo Justice Plan.

source.title: Atienden Plan de Justicia al pueblo Yoreme-Mayo de Sonora

facts.text: Yoreme patron saint fiestas strengthen the social networks that link communities across Mayo lands and keep Yoreme identity alive.

source.title: Mayos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Ute Mountain Ute Tribe
nations.lands: Towaoc and reservation lands in southwestern Colorado and northwestern New Mexico; White Mesa, Utah, United States

facts.text: The Ute Mountain Ute Tribe identifies itself as the Weenuche band of the Ute Nation, with its tribal offices in Towaoc, Colorado.
White Mesa Administration supports community members with employment, education and access to basic services in White Mesa, Utah.

nations.name: Comcaac
nations.lands: Desert coast of Sonora on the Gulf of California, Mexico, including Punta Chueca, El Desemboque and Tiburón Island

facts.text: In 1975 Mexico declared the Canal del Infiernillo an exclusive Comcaac fishing zone and symbolically granted them Tiburón Island, a nature reserve, as communal land.

source.title: Seris
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: Comcaac artisans weave coritas, baskets made since before Spanish contact. A very large one can take a year or two to finish.

source.title: Seris
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Hualapai
nations.lands: Northwestern Arizona, US, along the Grand Canyon and Colorado River (Peach Springs)

facts.text: The name Hualapai means People of the Tall Pines.
The Hualapai Reservation, set up in 1883, covers about one million acres along 108 miles of the Grand Canyon and Colorado River.

nations.name: Warihó and Macurawe
nations.lands: Foothills of the Sierra Madre Occidental on the Chihuahua and Sonora border, Mexico

facts.text: The people call themselves Macurawe in Sonora and Warihó in Chihuahua. Their Uto-Aztecan language has two variants and bridges Tarahumara and Mayo.

source.title: Guarijíos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: Warihó and Macurawe families weave baskets, mats and hats from palm and fiber and build harps, violins and guitars. Their craft work is family based and rests with women.

source.title: Guarijíos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Diné
nations.lands: Diné Bikéyah (Navajoland) across Arizona, New Mexico and Utah, US

facts.text: The Navajo Nation Council, the Nation’s governing body, has 24 delegates elected from legislative districts.
Diné Bikéyah, the Navajo Nation, covers more than 27,000 square miles across Arizona, New Mexico and Utah, larger than 10 of the 50 US states.

nations.name: Havasu Baaja
nations.lands: Havasu Canyon in the Grand Canyon, Arizona, US (village of Supai)

facts.text: Supai is so remote that the US Postal Service carries all mail in and out of the canyon by mule train.
The Havasupai reservation was set up in 1880 and greatly enlarged in 1975. It covers 188,077 acres beside the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.

nations.name: White Mountain Apache
nations.lands: White Mountains of east-central Arizona, US (Fort Apache Indian Reservation, Whiteriver)

facts.text: The White Mountain Apache own and run Sunrise, one of the largest ski resorts in the Southwest, and rare Apache trout swim in reservation streams.
White Mountain Apache people live on 1.6 million acres of their ancestral homeland, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, set aside in 1891.

nations.name: Tonto Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Payson, Gila County, Arizona, United States

facts.text: The Tonto Apache Tribe is based beside Payson in northwestern Gila County, Arizona.
In 2010, land for the Tonto Apache Tribe was acquired in trust following a land exchange with the U.S. Forest Service.

source.title: Reservation proclamation for trust land belonging to the Tonto Apache Tribe of Arizona

nations.name: Yavapai
nations.lands: Central and western Arizona, US, including Fort McDowell near Phoenix and Prescott

facts.text: In September 2026 the Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation, about 950 members, marked 123 years since its land was set aside in 1903.

source.title: Welcome to Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation

facts.text: In 1976 Fort McDowell Yavapai community members voted 144 to 57 against selling their land for the Orme Dam, and in 1981 the dam was called off.

nations.name: Ohkay Owingeh
nations.lands: Where the Rio Grande and Rio Chama meet, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: Ohkay Owingeh is the headquarters of the Eight Northern Pueblo Tribal Council.
The people have long called their home Ohkay Owingeh, place of the strong people in Tewa, and officially restored that name in place of San Juan, given in 1598.

nations.name: Cocopah
nations.lands: Lower Colorado River and delta: south of Yuma and near Somerton, Arizona, US, and the Mexicali valley of Baja California and San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora, Mexico

facts.text: About 1,000 Cocopah tribal members live and work on or near their reservation south of Yuma, Arizona, which was established in 1917.
Since 2003 the Cucapá of El Mayor, Baja California, and the Cocopah of Somerton, Arizona, have met each year with dances, songs, crafts and food.

source.title: Cucapás
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Nuche
nations.lands: Southwestern Colorado (Ignacio, Towaoc), northeastern Utah (Uintah and Ouray) and nearby New Mexico and Utah lands, US

facts.text: There are three Ute tribes today: the Southern Ute (Mouache and Capote bands), the Ute Mountain Ute (Weenuche band) and the Northern Ute in Utah.
The Ute Mountain Ute Tribe teaches the Ute language to Head Start children ages 2 to 5 and holds evening language classes for adults.

nations.name: Baniwa
nations.lands: Içana river and the Upper Rio Negro in Amazonas, Brazil, and neighboring Colombia and Venezuela

facts.text: The Baniwa speak languages of the Arawak family along the Içana river.
Baniwa communities live where Brazil meets Colombia and Venezuela, along the Içana river in the Upper Rio Negro region.

nations.name: Wapichana
nations.lands: Northeastern Roraima, Brazil, and the South Rupununi in southwestern Guyana

facts.text: In 2012 Wapichan leaders in Guyana presented a community map and land plan titled Thinking Together for those Coming Behind Us.

source.title: Wapichan people in Guyana present territorial map and community proposals to save ancestral forests

facts.text: The Wapichana language is classified in the Arawak language family.

nations.name: Guarani Mbya
nations.lands: Villages across southern and southeastern Brazil, eastern Paraguay, Misiones province in Argentina, and near Montevideo in Uruguay

facts.text: The Comissão Guarani Yvyrupa, founded in 2006, brings together Guarani collectives in six states of southern and southeastern Brazil.
In Guarani, yvyrupa names the structure that holds up the land, recalling free movement across territory before today's borders.

nations.name: Sápara
nations.lands: Rainforest of Pastaza province in the Ecuadorian Amazon, straddling the border with Peru

facts.text: The Sápara live in a part of the Amazon rainforest that straddles Ecuador and Peru.

source.title: Oral heritage and cultural manifestations of the Zápara people

facts.text: Sápara knowledge of the forest shows in their rich vocabulary for plants and animals and in their knowledge of the forest's medicinal plants.

source.title: Oral heritage and cultural manifestations of the Zápara people

nations.name: Kuikuro
nations.lands: Upper Xingu, in the Xingu Indigenous Territory, Mato Grosso, Brazil

facts.text: Kuikuro is a southern Carib language.
Kuikuro remains a living, intact language, used by everyone in all domains except talking with outsiders.

nations.name: Ka'apor
nations.lands: Northern Maranhão, Brazil, in the Alto Turiaçu Indigenous Land

facts.text: Ka'apor communities have had a shared, standard sign language for communicating with deaf members of the community.
Ka'apor is a language of the Tupi-Guarani family.

nations.name: A'uwe
nations.lands: Eastern Mato Grosso, Brazil, in Indigenous lands such as Pimentel Barbosa, Marãiwatsédé, São Marcos and Sangradouro

facts.text: The A'uwe (Xavante) language belongs to the Jê family of the Macro-Jê language stock.
The Xavante numbered about 22,256 people in 2020.

nations.name: Pataxó
nations.lands: Villages in the far south of Bahia and the north of Minas Gerais, Brazil

facts.text: The Pataxó are rebuilding their language, Patxohã, through a major community effort.
Pataxó villages are spread across the far south of Bahia and the north of Minas Gerais.

nations.name: Macuxi
nations.lands: Fields and mountains of northern Roraima, Brazil, between the headwaters of the Branco and Rupununi rivers, extending into Guyana and Venezuela

facts.text: The Conselho Indígena de Roraima, founded in 1990, unites ten peoples including the Macuxi and Wapichana, with 270 of the state's 465 communities as members.
The Macuxi language belongs to the Carib language family.

nations.name: Ashaninka
nations.lands: Upper Juruá region of Acre, Brazil, including the Amônia, Breu and Envira rivers, near the Peruvian border

facts.text: Ashaninka of the Amônia river created their own association, Apiwtxa, in 1991; it was officially registered in 1993.
Ashenĩka, the people's own name, can be translated as my relatives, my folk or my people.

nations.name: Terena
nations.lands: Mato Grosso do Sul, with communities in Mato Grosso and São Paulo, Brazil

facts.text: Farming remains the main productive activity in Terena reserves.
Terena people living in cities are concentrated mainly in Campo Grande, and most of them keep strong ties with their reserves.

nations.name: Tikuna
nations.lands: Along the upper Solimões (Amazon) river in Amazonas, Brazil, and in neighboring Peru and Colombia

facts.text: Tikuna communities are spread across three countries: Brazil, Peru and Colombia.
Tikuna is a tonal language, considered genetically isolated, with a complex sound system and grammar.

nations.name: Shuar
nations.lands: Zamora Chinchipe, Morona Santiago and southern Pastaza provinces in the Ecuadorian Amazon

facts.text: In 2022 the Shuar Aratsim Center approved its own Life Plan after participatory community workshops.

source.title: Territory of the Shuar People
source.publisher: ReVista, Harvard Review of Latin America (David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies)

facts.text: The Interprovincial Federation of Shuar Centers (FICSH), founded in 1964, was one of the pioneering Indigenous organizations of the Amazon.

source.title: Territory of the Shuar People
source.publisher: ReVista, Harvard Review of Latin America (David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies)

nations.name: Achuar
nations.lands: Northern Loreto in Peru near the Ecuador border, and the neighboring Amazon of Ecuador

facts.text: Peru's Ministry of Culture has registered five interpreters and translators of the Achuar language.

source.title: Achuar | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: Achuar is a cross-border language, spoken in both Peru and Ecuador.

source.title: Achuar | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Avá Guarani
nations.lands: Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná in Brazil, and eastern Paraguay

facts.text: Guarani peoples, the Avá Guarani among them, live across a territory that spans regions of Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina.
The Avá Guarani, called Ñandeva in Brazil, have a present-day territory that takes in parts of Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná.

source.title: Guarani Kaiowá - Povos Indígenas no Brasil

nations.name: Puyallup Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Shores of southern Puget Sound and the Puyallup River, Tacoma area, Washington

facts.text: One of the most urban tribes in the United States, the Puyallup still fish, hunt and travel the waters of the Puyallup River.
The Tribe gives its name as puyaləpabš, meaning people at the bend at the bottom of the river.

nations.name: Morongo Band of Mission Indians
nations.lands: Morongo Indian Reservation beneath the San Gorgonio Mountains, Riverside County, California

facts.text: Morongo tribal members elect a seven-member Tribal Council to lead their independent tribal government.
Established in 1865, the Morongo Indian Reservation now spans more than 35,000 acres.

nations.name: Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria
nations.lands: Sonoma and Marin counties, California, with a reservation near Rohnert Park

facts.text: Graton Rancheria launched its own Tribal TANF program serving low-income Native American families in Sonoma and Marin counties.
